articles.title: Malicious Tor Exit Nodes Compromised: SSH Traffic Redirected for MITM Attacks, Stealing Passwords and Installing Backdoors.
articles.excerpt: Introduction: The Tor Network Under Siege The Tor network, a critical infrastructure for online privacy and anonymity, operates by routing user traffic through a series of encrypted relays, obscuring…
articles.body: Introduction: The Tor Network Under Siege The Tor network, a critical infrastructure for online privacy and anonymity, operates by routing user traffic through a series of encrypted relays, obscuring both the origin and destination of data. This design has made it an indispensable tool for journalists, activists, and individuals in surveillance-heavy or repressive environments. However, the network’s security model relies on the integrity of its nodes, particularly exit nodes, which serve as the final hop in the Tor circuit. On October 2, this model was severely compromised when a malicious actor seized control of 333 Tor exit nodes , representing approximately 10% of the network’s total exit capacity .
articles.author: Ksenia Rudneva

articles.title: Dynamic SSH Key Authentication in MuleSoft SFTP on CloudHub 2.0
articles.excerpt: If you've worked with SFTP integrations in MuleSoft, you've probably dealt with SSH private keys. Configuring a static key is relatively straightforward. But what happens when your MuleSoft applicatio…
articles.body: If you've worked with SFTP integrations in MuleSoft, you've probably dealt with SSH private keys. Configuring a static key is relatively straightforward. But what happens when your MuleSoft application connects to multiple partners, each with different credentials and regularly rotating SSH keys? Hardcoding those credentials isn't a scalable approach. This article explores a practical design pattern for dynamic SSH key authentication in MuleSoft SFTP on CloudHub 2.0, including temporary key storage, secure cleanup, and concurrency considerations. The Problem with Dynamic SSH Keys MuleSoft's SFTP Connector supports SSH private-key authentication, but the identity key configuration expects a filesystem path.

articles.title: Updating text at the cursor as a transcript changes, without retyping the whole thing
articles.excerpt: Disclosure: I'm the developer of Bolo, the app this code comes from, and this post is published from my account. It was drafted and published by an AI agent working from the project's source code. Bol…
articles.body: Disclosure: I'm the developer of Bolo, the app this code comes from, and this post is published from my account. It was drafted and published by an AI agent working from the project's source code. Bolo turns an Android phone into a wireless microphone for a Windows PC: you speak, and the words appear at the PC cursor in whatever app is focused. The hard part isn't the final text. It's the live preview — the partial transcript that updates several times a second while you're still talking, each version a little different from the last. Naively, every partial means: delete what you typed, type the new version. That is slow, it flickers, and over Remote Desktop the deletes and types arrive out of order and scramble. Here is how the Windows companion (Node.js) avoids all three.

articles.title: What I Automate First in a New Project, and Why It Is Never the Important Part
articles.excerpt: When I start working in a new repo or a new environment, there is a temptation to automate the interesting thing first. I have learned to resist it, and the order I use instead looks almost backwards.…
articles.body: When I start working in a new repo or a new environment, there is a temptation to automate the interesting thing first. I have learned to resist it, and the order I use instead looks almost backwards. The order The thing I run to find out where I am. Branch, dirty files, running services, last commit, what changed yesterday. This is not work, it is orientation, and I run it five times a day. The thing I run after every change. The build, the tests, the linter, whatever is fast enough to run constantly. The thing I run before I ask a human. The check that tells me whether my change does what I think. Only then the actual task that made me open the project. The first three are not the interesting part of the project.

articles.body: Just swap with other developers" is the most common advice for Google Play's closed testing rule, and it is good advice. It is also usually given without the price tag. Free testers are not free. You pay with your own time, every day, for at least 14 days. Here is what that actually costs, using the real numbers from PeerPlay's free exchange, what you get in return beyond the tester count, and the cases where paying is the smarter choice. The daily math For newer personal developer accounts, Google requires at least 12 testers opted in to your closed test for 14 days in a row before you can apply for production. In a 1-for-1 exchange, one tester for you means one app you test for someone else. So 12 testers means 12 apps on your phone.

articles.title: Don't type into a window someone is using: a cross-platform idle gate in Node.js
articles.excerpt: Disclosure: I'm the developer of the tool described here, and this post was drafted and published by an AI agent from the project's source code. Relaymote is unofficial; not affiliated with or endorse…
articles.body: Disclosure: I'm the developer of the tool described here, and this post was drafted and published by an AI agent from the project's source code. Relaymote is unofficial; not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic. Relaymote (MIT, Node.js) is my phone remote for Claude Desktop's Code-tab sessions. Some of what it does on the desktop is UI automation: it drives the window to approve a prompt or paste a message. That is fine at 2 a.m. when nobody is there. It is not fine if it fires while you are typing into the same window, because your keystrokes and its keystrokes interleave into one scrambled mess. So before any UI action, Relaymote asks one question: has the user provably been away for N seconds? This post is the small module that answers it, and the one rule that makes it safe.

articles.title: Verbs beat adjectives on a CV
articles.excerpt: Adjectives are claims. Verbs are events. When you write that a system was robust, scalable, and fast, you have told the parser and the reviewer nothing they have not read on every other application in…
articles.body: Adjectives are claims. Verbs are events. When you write that a system was robust, scalable, and fast, you have told the parser and the reviewer nothing they have not read on every other application in the pile. You have used words that require subjective interpretation. When you write that a system sustained three million daily requests after the query layer was migrated, you have stated an event. Reviewers and automated parsers look for the shape of work. They look for what changed because you were in the room. A strong verb paired with a hard metric does this work cleanly. It removes the need for persuasion. Take a standard bullet point and look at the load-bearing words. If the first word is managed, coordinated, or assisted, the sentence is hiding the actual labor.

The similarities to The Hobbit and LOTR pretty much end there though, and you don’t get nearly enough detail in the first book to effectively flesh out this alternate version of Middle-earth. articles.title: SpaceX will attempt 1st-ever double Starship rocket catch on next test launch, a 'profound technology milestone,' Elon Musk says
articles.excerpt: SpaceX will try to recover both Starship stages during the megarocket's next test flight, which is expected to take place in November, according to Elon Musk.
articles.body: SpaceX will soon notch a huge spaceflight milestone, if all goes according to plan. The company will try to catch both stages of its Starship megarocket during the vehicle's next test flight, which is targeted for next month, founder and CEO Elon Musk announced during SpaceX's quarter 3 (Q3) earnings call today (Oct. 20). If SpaceX succeeds, this "will be the first time that an orbital launch vehicle has been fully recovered," Musk said. With this update, Gemini in Android Auto and cars with Google built-in can tap into your information across Google apps, including Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, YouTube, and Search. articles.body: Tesla and SpaceX have formed special committees to discuss a possible merger, Elon Musk said during the latter's third quarter earnings call Tuesday .
